title: Dev-focused status note + SDK retry snippets for customers
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, developer-facing status + customer note template for incidents that manifest as elevated queue latency / throttling or transient stale responses. Intended for engineering teams who embed Redwood SDKs and want copy-and-paste guidance for status pages plus lightweight SDK retry examples that mitigate visible customer impact.

Audience:
- Primary: engineering leads at customers (platform, backend)
- Secondary: product/ops contacts who need a short, actionable summary for their downstream teams

Intended use:
- Quick status page snippet to post while operators are triaging (5 lines max)
- Follow-up customer-facing one-pager with timeline and verification steps
- Small SDK/psuedocode snippets customers can drop into services to reduce error surface during a rolling recovery

Notes on tone and priorities:
- Plain English, no internal jargon (avoid: "ingress shard", "KV cache eviction" unless customer has asked)
- Emphasize what customers can do (retry knobs, idempotency, safe fallbacks)
- Provide a minimal verification checklist so customers can confirm integrity locally

Suggested short status page snippet (60–120 chars):
- "We’re investigating increased inference latency in US regions. No data loss. Working on routing and capacity — updates in 30m."
- Quick variants (for page updates):
  - 5m update: "Mitigation in progress — additional routing capacity enabled; some requests still delayed."
  - 30m update: "Latency improving; customers on SDK v>=0.9.2 see automatic backoff-handling. Continue to report anomalies."

Developer-facing one-paragraph status (for customers who want technical context):
- "What happened: A rapid surge of long-sequence requests triggered sustained queueing on a subset of GPU pools, causing increased end-to-end latency and a small number of stale-looking responses while requests were served from fallback model variants. Impact: higher response times and occasional truncated/partial outputs for a subset of requests. Mitigation: we routed traffic away from affected pools, increased reserved capacity, and applied a cache clear to reduce stale KV artifacts. No customer data was deleted or exposed. Next: rolling validation and targeted replays for affected tenants who request them."

Post-incident one-pager skeleton (customer-facing):
- Title: "Quick post-incident note — increased inference latency (US-East) — <DATE>"
- 1-sentence summary: short human sentence of impact and customer action (if any)
- What we observed: bullet timeline (operator times)
- Root cause (short): what subsystem behaved unexpectedly
- What we did to fix it: actions taken, order (routing change, capacity, cache clear, model pin rollback)
- Customer verification steps: short checks (see below)
- Replay / remediation options: opt-in guidance if customers want reprocessing
- Contact & escalation: named CSM + support link

Minimal timeline example (copyable):
- 09:08 UTC — first metric alert: US-e2 latency p90 > 800ms
- 09:12 UTC — detected queue depth spike on pool-gpu-12
- 09:20 UTC — enabled fallback routing to spare pools (partial mitigation)
- 09:33 UTC — applied cache clear on affected nodes
- 09:50 UTC — p95 and p99 returned to baseline; ongoing monitoring

Customer verification checklist (1–3 quick checks):
- Can you reproduce high latency on the same tenant key? (yes/no)
- If you have logs, do you see repeated 429/503 from Redwood endpoints between <start> and <end>?
- Run a small sample: call Redwood with same prompt and sequence length; confirm response latency and content sanity.

Opt-in replay flow (customer choices):
- If customers want affected requests re-run for consistency-sensitive workloads, they can:
  1) Provide time window + tenant id + request ids (optional) in the support ticket
  2) Choose: (A) best-effort re-run (no cost) or (B) curated re-run with integrity verification (small fee; deliverable: sample output and hash comparisons)

Copy snippets for status page (short, mid, closure):
- Initial: "We’re investigating elevated inference latency in US regions. No customer data deleted. Updates in 30 minutes."
- Mid: "Routing improvements deployed; bulk of traffic routed to spare capacity. Some developers may see intermittent delays; we’re validating outputs."
- Closure: "Service restored to normal. Root cause identified and fixed; optional replay available on request. Full customer postmortem to follow."

SDK retry example (pseudocode) — drop-in (JS/Go/Python examples)
- Principles: exponential backoff, small jitter, idempotency key when possible, re-check for stale content rather than blind retry (if your app can tolerate)

JS (node) pseudo:
- const MAX = 5
- async function callWithRetry(req) {
    let attempt = 0
    while (attempt < MAX) {
      try {
        return await rwClient.generate(req)
      } catch (e) {
        if (!isTransient(e) || attempt === MAX-1) throw e
        await sleep((2 ** attempt) * 100 + randomJitter())
        attempt++
      }
    }
  }

Python pseudo:
- def call_with_retry(req):
    for attempt in range(5):
        try:
            return client.generate(req)
        except TransientError as e:
            if attempt == 4:
                raise
            time.sleep((2**attempt)*0.1 + jitter())

Key SDK knobs to highlight to customers:
- set max_tokens/sequence_length to expected for workload (avoid accidental long sequences)
- enable client-side client_retry/backoff if using long-prompt flows
- use model pinning to avoid surprise model swaps (if strict determinism needed)
- enable response-hash in headers to help verify replays

Sample support ticket template for customers who want a replay:
- Subject: Replay request — latency incident <DATE>
- Body: Tenant ID: <tid>
        Time window: <start> to <end> (UTC)
        Request ids (if available): <list>
        Preferred replay mode: best-effort / verified

Open questions for internal review (note section):
- Should we auto-surface code snippets in status pages or keep them in follow-up customer notes?
- Do we want a standard header to request idempotency keys from customers who want replays?
- Are we comfortable offering free best-effort replays for all tiers? (policy + cost implications)

Links & refs:
- SDK retry PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-sdk/pull/198
- Incident tracking: https://linear.app/RD/issue/INF-4327
- Slack thread: #customer-ops (G9F2K4L)

Draft checklist before posting to status page:
- [ ] Confirm wording with SRE lead (Ethan Park)
- [ ] Validate no customer-facing PII in timelines
- [ ] Confirm replay policy with CS manager (Sofia Alvarez)
- [ ] Add support ticket template and link to status update

Notes to self / shorthand:
- Keep initial message tight — engineers prefer short and actionable
- Provide SDK snippets in follow-up doc rather than first-minute status page unless request comes from dev contact
- If asked by customer, provide sample cURL + SDK call with response-hash header for verification

End of draft.
